Vitamin D2 raised 25(OH)D much more than placebo did. None of the four fibrosis markers changed differently between the arms at alpha 0.05.

To answer the review: the value −2176.83 ng/mL is the minimum of the MMP_change column. It comes from the column summary of the first data check (inspect_table, file columns.csv). The dot plot shows that this lowest value belongs to a placebo patient. I now name this source in the text.

**Method.** I used an unpaired Student t-test (equal variances, two-sided, alpha 0.05) on each change from baseline. These settings came from the decision record. One replicate is one patient. The data hold 75 patients with one row each and no missing values: 37 vitamin D2 and 38 placebo. Each estimate is the mean change in the vitamin D arm minus the mean change in the placebo arm, in ng/mL. The effect size is Cohen's d. The Holm correction covers all 5 tests. Because each outcome is already a change from baseline, I did not adjust for the baseline value.

**Results (step: compare two groups, then adjust p-values)**

| Outcome | Mean change, placebo | Mean change, vitamin D | Difference (vit D − placebo) | 95% CI | p (raw) | p (Holm) | Cohen's d |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 25(OH)D | 1.497 | 24.584 | **23.09** | 19.73 to 26.44 | 6.6 × 10⁻²² | 3.3 × 10⁻²¹ | 3.17 |
| TGF-beta1 | 1.032 | 0.477 | **−0.554** | −2.839 to 1.731 | 0.630 | 1.0 | −0.11 |
| TIMP-1 | 12.624 | 7.114 | **−5.51** | −26.36 to 15.34 | 0.600 | 1.0 | −0.12 |
| MMP-9 | −14.86 | 108.06 | **122.92** | −68.96 to 314.81 | 0.206 | 0.823 | 0.29 |
| P3NP | −0.814 | −0.925 | **−0.110** | −2.372 to 2.151 | 0.923 | 1.0 | −0.02 |

For each test, t had 73 degrees of freedom: 13.72 for 25(OH)D, −0.48 for TGF-beta1, −0.53 for TIMP-1, 1.28 for MMP-9 and −0.10 for P3NP.

- **25(OH)D:** the increase is significant at alpha 0.05, before and after the Holm correction.
- **Fibrosis markers:** no difference in mean change is significant at alpha 0.05, before or after correction.
- **Width of the intervals:** the TIMP-1 and MMP-9 intervals are wide, so the data cannot rule out moderate effects in either direction.
